claim: On 9 October 2025 China's Unreliable Entity List working mechanism (notice 〔2025〕 No. 10) listed 14 entries: 13 named foreign organisations (including Dedrone by Axon, BAE Systems, Inc., Teledyne FLIR, Recorded Future and the Halifax International Security Forum) and TechInsights Inc. with nine affiliates (three of them Strategy Analytics entities), banning them from China-related import/export and new investment in China and banning Chinese parties from transacting with them, especially sending them data.
evidence: "决定将反无人机技术公司、TechInsights公司及其分支机构等外国实体列入不可靠实体清单" ... list items 1-13 (incl. "12. Recorded Future公司", "13. 哈利法克斯国际安全论坛") and "14. TechInsights公司（TechInsights Inc.）及其分支机构" with 10 sub-lines incl. SARL Strategy Analytics. (Annex)
notes: Fact-check correction of CLM-1407: the notice does not call the other 13 'US defence-related'; it gives no nationality, and Recorded Future (threat intelligence) and the Halifax International Security Forum are not defence manufacturers. 13 + TechInsights Inc. + 9 affiliates = 23 entities.

claim: MOFCOM control-list notices 2026 Nos. 23 (22 June), 27 (29 June) and 30 (24 July) ban both exporters' exports and any foreign organisation or individual from transferring Chinese-origin dual-use items to the listed entities, whereas 2025 Nos. 1 (2 January) and 13 (4 March) banned only exports to the listed entities; the date the wider wording first appeared was not established.
evidence: 2026 No. 27: "禁止出口经营者向上述20家实体出口两用物项，禁止境外组织和个人将原产于中华人民共和国的两用物项转移或提供给上述20家实体"; 2025 No. 1: "一、禁止向上述28家美国实体出口两用物项"; 2025 No. 13: "一、禁止向上述15家美国实体出口两用物项".
notes: Fact-check narrowing of CLM-1413 ('since 2026' not established: notices between April 2025 and June 2026 were not audited). Inference from CLM-1411, CLM-1412 and the notices cited.

claim: MOFCOM extended its trade-barrier investigation into US practices that damage global supply chains (opened 27 March 2026) to 27 December 2026, citing the complexity of the case.
evidence: "鉴于案情复杂，根据《对外贸易壁垒调查规则》第三十二条规定，商务部决定将上述两起调查期限均延长至2026年12月27日。" (Xinhua, 30 Sep 2026)
notes: Updates the timeline in CLM-1430. The MOFCOM extension notice itself was not opened (Xinhua report only).

claim: Fangda Partners said MOFCOM Announcement 2026 No. 21 (2 May 2026) was the first time since the Blocking Rules were issued on 9 January 2021 that MOFCOM found a foreign measure to be improperly extraterritorial and issued a blocking prohibition.
evidence: "这是自2021年1月9日《阻断办法》公布以来，中国商务部第一次宣布外国法律法规存在不当域外适用情形，并发布阻断禁令要求不得承认、不得执行、不得遵守外国制裁措施。" (Fangda, 6 May 2026)
notes: Law-firm commentary (tier 3); supports the 'first' qualifier in CLM-1418, which the MOFCOM notice itself does not state.

claim: USGS reported that in November 2025 China lifted its ban on gallium exports to the United States for one year.
evidence: "In November 2025, China lifted its ban on gallium exports to the United States for 1 year. This followed the Government of China's gallium export controls implemented in August 2023 and China's ban of all gallium exports to the United States in December 2024." (MCS 2026, Gallium, Events, Trends, and Issues)
notes: Corresponds legally to the suspension of para. 2 of Announcement 2024 No. 46 until 27 November 2026 (CLM-1385); USGS's 'lifted ... for 1 year' is a simplification of a suspension.

claim: USGS's Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026 again stated that China accounted for 99% of world primary low-purity gallium production.
evidence: "China accounted for 99% of worldwide primary low-purity gallium production. The remaining primary low-purity gallium producers outside of China included Japan and Russia." (MCS 2026, Gallium)

metric.name: China share of world primary low-purity gallium production

notes: Newer edition of CLM-1442; the share is unchanged. Korea no longer listed as a producer in MCS 2026.

claim: USGS Open-File Report 2024-1057 estimated that a complete restriction of China's net exports of gallium and germanium (2022 baseline) would raise rest-of-world gallium prices more than 2.5-fold and germanium prices by 26%, and cut US GDP by USD 3.4 billion (range USD 1.7-9.0 billion) if both were disrupted at the same time.
evidence: "a complete restriction of China's net exports of gallium ... would cause gallium prices in the rest of the world to increase by more than 2.5-fold" ... "would cause germanium prices to increase by 26 percent" ... "$3.4 billion ($1.7 billion to $9.0 billion) if disrupted simultaneously." (OFR 2024-1057, Abstract and Results)

metric.name: Estimated US GDP loss from complete restriction of China's net Ga and Ge exports
metric.methodology: USGS price-equilibrium model plus input-output (BEA) economic model

notes: Primary-source version of CLM-1443 (which cites Stimson second-hand). Separate disruptions: gallium USD 3.1 bn (1.7-8.2), germanium USD 0.4 bn (0.01-1.1). Baseline China net exports 2022: Ga 159 t of 638 t world output; Ge 35 t of 210 t.
